title: Cucumber and Coriander Raita
summary: Whole-milk yoghurt with salted, squeezed cucumber, fresh coriander, a little green chilli and a pinch of cayenne, served well chilled.

ingredients.item: fine sea salt or table salt
fresh coriander, finely chopped, plus a few leaves to serve
fine sea salt or table salt

steps.title: Salt the cucumber
steps.text: Coarsely grate the cucumber into the sieve, sprinkle with 0.25 tsp salt, toss and leave for 15 min. The salt pulls out excess water so the raita stays creamy.

steps.title: Squeeze it out
steps.text: Bundle the cucumber in the tea towel and twist firmly over the sink until little more liquid drips out. If you want a garnish like the photo, slice a few thin rounds from the cucumber before grating.

steps.title: Season the yoghurt
steps.text: Whisk the yoghurt in the bowl until smooth and slightly loosened, then stir in the cayenne and the remaining salt. Fold in the cucumber, chopped coriander and green chilli.

steps.title: Chill
steps.text: Cover and refrigerate for at least 20 min so it is properly cold and the flavours come together.

steps.title: Finish and serve
steps.text: Spoon into a serving bowl and top with a few coriander leaves and the cucumber slices. Serve alongside curry, rice dishes or kebabs.

tips: Whole-milk yoghurt gives the best body; low-fat versions turn thin once the cucumber goes in.
Leave the chilli out for children or anyone sensitive to heat; the cayenne still adds a gentle warmth.
A pinch of toasted ground cumin stirred in at the end adds a nutty, smoky edge.
Make it no more than a few hours ahead for the crispest cucumber.
storage: Keep covered in the fridge for up to 2 days and stir before serving. Not suitable for freezing. Cool leftovers in a shallow container and refrigerate within 2 hours (within 1 hour on a day above 32°C).
